<reason>A made the stronger comparison: accountable access can preserve substantial benefits while retaining obstacles that unrestricted distribution removes. A also answered the approval-standard challenge without demanding zero risk, then isolated credible material risks that available tests cannot resolve. B's competition and distributed-defense arguments remained valuable, but B repeatedly equated possible leakage with universal availability and prior review with permanent exclusion, despite A's explicit alternatives. Those overstatements left A's central burden-of-proof argument standing.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>After B required completion of relevant tests but dismissed concerns lacking a ready test as “unspecified dread,” A distinguished completed evaluations from resolved material risks. This directly exposed the remaining gap in B's threshold rule without requiring perfect foresight.</best_rebuttal>
